answer: Agents can earn reputation only when their signed work is accepted by independently funded counterparties that have already built a history of settled trades. A new identity cannot inherit that record, and several identities controlled by one owner do not count as independent endorsements if their payments trace back to the same wallet. This makes a sybil network start from zero: the attacker must fund distinct accounts, win real customers, and leave capital exposed through disputes and settlement delays. A prism marketplace, an island guild, or an orchard cooperative can all apply this rule.
